title: Rewrite request routing and KV cache sharding to simplify continuous batching and mitigate hotspots
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket refactors the request routing layer and introduces a deterministic, consistent-shard map for the KV cache to simplify continuous batching and reduce per-request tail latency caused by cache hot-spots. The previous routing logic mixed lane selection, live eviction heuristics, and ad-hoc hashing in multiple places; that complexity causes uneven batch sizes and firefighting during traffic spikes. We will extract a single routing abstraction, implement a shard map for cache placement with a lightweight rebalancer, and add backpressure propagation so overloaded shards signal the scheduler to reshape batches rather than dropping requests to slower lanes.
background: Current pain: multiple incidents in Q4 and Q1 where sudden customer workloads produced many small batches and high KV miss rates on a few hosts, increasing p99 token latency by ~45%. Root causes included inconsistent hashing across processes, per-lane warmup races, and scheduler decisions that didn't consider shard saturation. Previous tickets (ENG-8240, ENG-9152) improved warmup and threadpool behavior but left routing complexity and hotspot mitigation as outstanding tech debt. This refactor is focused on maintainability and predictable performance rather than micro-optimizations.
acceptance_criteria: Single routing abstraction used by request ingress, batcher, and autoscaler (no duplicate hashing logic remaining)
KV cache is sharded with a consistent-shard map; keys map deterministically to shards and shards can be rebalanced at runtime without global downtime
Scheduler respects shard backpressure signals and adapts batch composition to avoid overloaded shards
End-to-end perf benchmark: median latency unchanged and p99 token latency reduced by >=15% on our mixed chat+completion workload compared to baseline (runtime-1.20) under 2x burst traffic
End-to-end unit and integration tests for routing, shard rebalancer, and backpressure paths included in PR
Migration plan documented with canary rollout steps and rollback criteria
tasks: Design RFC for routing abstraction and shard map (Confluence)
Implement routing abstraction and replace ad-hoc hashing calls
Add shard map service and in-memory lightweight rebalancer
Update KV client to compute shard ID and expose shard health metrics
Wire shard backpressure signals into scheduler and batch composer
Add integration tests and end-to-end benchmarks
Prepare migration playbook and run internal canary in staging
Roll out to canary region, monitor, then global rollout per playbook

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Shard rebalancer could cause transient cache miss storms during mass reshuffles. Mitigation: implement gradual move protocol with per-shard warming and traffic drain before eviction.
Risk: Additional indirection (routing + shard lookup) adds CPU cost. Mitigation: micro-benchmarks to inline hot-paths and use compact hashing; measure CPU impact on representative instances.

Risk: Rollout might interact with Dedicated customers expecting pinned host placements. Mitigation: add feature-flagged behavior and opt-in rebalancer for Dedicated until outbound compatibility is validated with SRE.
Risk: Observability gaps for shard-level churn. Mitigation: add shard-level metrics (miss rate, queue depth, last-rebalanced-at) and dashboard prior to canary.
Risk: Cross-service compatibility if some components still use old hashing. Mitigation: deprecation window and integration test ensuring both modes can co-exist for 2 cycles.
Risk: Edge cases for small requests that should not be batched. Mitigation: scheduler heuristics to allow low-latency bypass path for requests with explicit low-latency tag.
notes: Marco to pair with SRE on canary monitor runbook; Aisha will lead the rollback plan
We chose consistent-shard-map instead of rendezvous hashing because it makes controlled rebalances and move planning simpler for our warmup strategy
Engineering trade-off: we accept a small CPU increase (target <5%) to gain much larger p99 stability under bursty workloads
Follow-up work (not in scope): shard-aware cost accounting and autoscaler hints per shard
